did_you_know.text: Did you know? Four officials—Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah—heard Jeremiah speaking to the people and later took action against him.

Did you know? The officials claimed that Jeremiah’s words were weakening the hands of the soldiers and the people because he was urging them to surrender to the Chaldeans rather than continue resisting in the besieged city.
Did you know? Jeremiah was thrown into a cistern in the courtyard of the guard. There was no water in it, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into it.

Did you know? Ebed-melech the Cushite heard that Jeremiah had been thrown into the cistern, even though he was in the king’s palace, and took action to rescue him. He is described as a eunuch, and the king was sitting at the Gate of Benjamin at that time.
Did you know? When Jeremiah was lifted out of the cistern, Ebed-melech made sure that the ropes were padded with worn-out rags and old clothes so they would not hurt him under his arms.
Did you know? Zedekiah summoned Jeremiah for a secret meeting at the third entrance to the house of the LORD and asked him not to hide anything from him.

Did you know? Jeremiah told Zedekiah the LORD’s conditions: if he surrendered to the officials of the king of Babylon, he, his household, and the city would live and the city would not be burned; but if he refused, the city would be handed over to the Chaldeans and burned.

Did you know? After his conversation with Zedekiah, Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured, bringing the chapter to a close against the backdrop of the city’s approaching conquest.
